generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The abstract method `dropLargeFields()` declares `throws Exception`, but neither implementation (`MessageWatchRecord` or `ExceptionWatchRecord`) throws any checked exception — they simply construct new objects. This forces callers to either catch a meaningless `Exception` or declare it, which is misleading. If no implementation currently throws a checked exception, the `throws` clause should be removed. If there's a realistic possibility of `IOException` in future implementations, `throws IOException` would be the appropriate bound.

Minor inconsistency: `triggerEvent` is referenced without the `this.` prefix while every other field in the same constructor call uses `this.`. Compare with the identical pattern in `#TDW46` where `this.triggerEvent` is used. This is a small style inconsistency but worth aligning for readability.

The truncation logic serializes the full record first (to build the `IndexRequest`), checks the byte length, and only then re-serializes a truncated version. For a record that is, say, 500 MB, this means the full 500 MB is serialized into memory before being discarded. Consider serializing to a `BytesReference` first and checking its length before constructing the `IndexRequest`, or at minimum adding a log statement when truncation is triggered so operators can observe it happening.

The `verify(client, atLeastOnce()).bulk(any(), any())` calls are weak assertions — they will pass as long as *any* prior `bulk` call was made, regardless of whether the current `put()` actually triggered one. Using `verify(client, times(n)).bulk(any(), any())` with an incrementing counter (or `verify(client, timeout(1000).times(n))`) would make the test more precise and catch cases where `put()` silently fails to enqueue.

review_comment: I'm also assuming that adding a new field to the history store doesn't need any further changes to mappings or anything?

It looks like `input` doesn't specify dynamic, so it defaults to dynamic (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/watch-history.json#L108). And `result` is explicitly dynamic (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/core/template-resources/src/main/resources/watch-history.json#L136).
